_DESIGN_RULE: The deck holds NOTHING but Trust cards. Products are not in here - they sit in an always-visible tray, because v2 measured 12 of 26 deck slots as dead weight you could not legally play until you had diagnosed something. There are no Question cards either: crossing a Trust threshold reveals a need by itself, so building Trust IS asking. That leaves Trust exactly two outlets, and every card below is one of them: raise it (Small Talk, Genuine Connection, Common Ground) or cash it out for Patience (Reassure). Any new card must be one of those two things, or it is a third job for Trust and the model stops being legible. Cards cost 1 ACTION by default - the shared action budget across the whole floor is the triage puzzle. Small Talk is the ONE deliberate exception at 0 actions: it is the cheap tempo card that lets you touch a second customer in a round you had already committed elsewhere. Note what a 0-action card is and is not - it is never a question of WHETHER to play it, only of WHO gets it, so keep such cards weak enough that the who is the whole decision. A 0-action card strong enough to be the main way you build Trust would delete the triage puzzle outright.

cards.name: Small Talk
cards.text: +2 Trust, and it costs no action. Free to play, so the only question is who gets it - use it to nudge someone over a threshold in a round you spent elsewhere.

cards.name: Genuine Connection
cards.text: +4 Trust. Bread and butter - one of these clears most first reveals outright.

cards.name: Common Ground
cards.text: +2 Trust to EVERY customer still on the floor. Rewards spreading attention instead of tunnelling one customer.

cards.name: Reassure
cards.text: Spend 3 Trust to buy 5 Patience. Never un-reveals what you already learned, but it does throw away progress toward the next reveal - and it buys far fewer rounds on a fast burner.
